seo_meta_description: Master Quadratics on the Digital SAT using built-in Desmos graphing calculator hacks, syntax commands, regressions, and speed drills.
exam_weightage: Essential Digital SAT Tool (5-8 Questions per Module)

techniques.title: Interactive Sliders for Unknown Constants
techniques.description: Define an equation with variables like 'a', 'b', or 'k'. Desmos will create 'add slider' buttons. Adjust sliders to match the graph to given points or conditions.
techniques.when_to_use: When a problem asks for a constant that makes a parabola pass through specific points or have a specific vertex.
techniques.pro_tip: Click the slider value to type exact numbers for precision.

techniques.title: Regression Formula for Best Fit
techniques.description: Input a table of values and use the tilde (~) operator to find the quadratic equation that fits the data perfectly.
techniques.when_to_use: When given a table of (x, y) values and asked for the quadratic model.
techniques.pro_tip: Use the 'residuals' plot to verify if the fit is perfect (residuals should be 0).

techniques.title: Finding Intersections with Clickable Points
techniques.description: Graph both equations; Desmos automatically highlights intersection points in grey. Click them to see coordinates.
techniques.when_to_use: Solving systems of equations involving a parabola and a line.
techniques.pro_tip: If points don't appear, zoom out or check if the equations are entered correctly.

techniques.title: Vertex and Intercept Identification
techniques.description: Graph the function; click the graph to see the grey dots representing the vertex and x-intercepts.
techniques.when_to_use: Questions asking for the maximum/minimum value, zeros, or roots.

techniques.title: Evaluating Expressions with Variables
techniques.description: Define the function using f(x), then type f(n) to evaluate the quadratic at any value n.
techniques.when_to_use: When asked to find the value of a quadratic expression for a specific input.
techniques.pro_tip: Use this to quickly check if an answer choice matches the function value.

speed_walkthroughs.problem: The function $f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 8$ is graphed in the $xy$-plane. What is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex?
desmos_hack: Step 2: Click the grey dot at the bottom of the parabola.
Step 3: Read the x-coordinate from the coordinate pair.

drills.question: Which of the following is equivalent to $2x^2 + 8x + 6$?
explanation: Step 2: Graph each option one by one.
Step 3: The option that perfectly overlaps the original graph is the equivalent expression.

drills.question: What is the positive solution to $x^2 - 5x - 14 = 0$?
explanation: Step 3: Identify the positive value among the intercepts.
